standard.title: Grid coordinate system
standard.description: Construct a grid coordinate system that uses coordinates to locate positions within a space; use coordinates and directional language to describe position and movement
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use grid reference systems (letter-number) to locate positions (AC9M4SP02). They have not yet used a coordinate system with ordered pairs or distinguished between the two coordinate axes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students construct a grid coordinate system and use coordinates and directional language to locate positions and describe movement.

nodes.label: From grid references to coordinates
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish a grid reference (letter-number cell) from a coordinate pair (point on intersecting lines) and explain the difference.
nodes.minimum_width: Plot a point using a coordinate pair on a prepared grid; explain the difference from a letter-number grid reference.
nodes.typical_width: Plot and read multiple coordinate points; explain that coordinates identify intersections not cells; connect to map and screen coordinate systems.
wider: Compare grid reference and coordinate systems used in different mapping tools
Investigate how First Nations navigation systems describe position and movement

response_modes.reason: Students often confuse (x, y) points with cell references. Maps, digital tools and design contexts provide multiple concrete representations that distinguish the two systems.

nodes.hinge_reason: The cell-vs-intersection distinction is the prerequisite for Node 2 — students who confuse grid references with coordinate pairs cannot construct a valid coordinate system or plot points accurately.
success_criteria: Student plots a coordinate pair correctly on a grid
Student explains the distinction between a grid reference and a coordinate pair

nodes.label: Constructing a coordinate grid
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a coordinate grid system with labelled axes for a given space.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw and label a coordinate grid with x- and y-axes, origin and at least 6 grid points; plot three given coordinates.
nodes.typical_width: Construct a coordinate grid for a practical purpose (e.g. mapping a classroom, game board); plot and read coordinates accurately.
wider: Extend to negative coordinates in one quadrant
Use coordinate grids in digital contexts: spreadsheet cell coordinates, screen pixel positions
success_criteria: Student constructs a correctly labelled coordinate grid
Student plots and reads coordinates accurately on their grid

nodes.label: Describing position and movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use coordinates and directional language to describe a position and a movement between positions.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the position of a point using its coordinates; describe a movement from one point to another using directional language.
nodes.typical_width: Describe routes on a coordinate grid using coordinates and directional language; describe movement in terms of changes in x and y values.
wider: Program directional movement on a coordinate grid using code or robotics
Design a coordinate treasure map with movement instructions

response_modes.reason: Coding and treasure map contexts vary the purpose and form of coordinate use, giving advancing students genuine breadth beyond abstract plotting exercises.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Coding movement on a grid and treasure map design give advancing students purposeful, rich application contexts.
success_criteria: Student describes a position using correct coordinate notation
Student describes movement between two points using directional language and coordinate changes
